scenes.title: Inspect groups and their hierarchy
scenes.narration: Open the department menu and choose Stations and Groups. The table separates each group’s type, parent, and member count. Our fictional Chicago Fire department already has a station and organizational groups beneath it. We will add an empty coordination parent and a separate station beneath that parent. Read the existing rows first so the new exercise is easy to identify and the original memberships remain intact.

scenes.title: Prepare an organizational parent
scenes.narration: Choose Add New Group and keep Organizational Group selected. Enter Training Only, Community Coordination, followed by the exercise date. Parent Group remains None, making this a top-level group. Group Admins and Group Users stay empty. These fields describe different membership responsibilities; choosing an administrator is a permission decision. We are preparing a structure, so we do not move a person from an existing group or assign an administrator.

scenes.title: Prepare a station under the new parent
scenes.narration: Create another group and select Station Group. Name it Training Only, Community Base, with the exercise date, and choose the new coordination group as its parent. A station requires a physical reference location. The form offers address fields, a coordinate pair, or a what3words address. We will use an explicitly illustrative Chicago coordinate pair. The parent describes the organizational relationship; it does not replace the station’s own location.

Keep the member and administrator selectors empty and leave printing unconfigured. Use Save Group once after checking the prepared values.

scenes.title: Separate a unit definition from its crew
scenes.narration: Open Units and choose New Unit. The form separates Name, Type, Station, and the unit’s role positions. No Station is available, but our exercise will use the station we just created. A role position defines a seat; it does not select the person occupying that seat. Before completing this unit, use the type link to create a distinct training vehicle type that will be recognizable in the unit list.

The optional custom-icon file remains empty. These choices define the new type without changing an existing type or a department status set.

scenes.title: Define two distinct positions
scenes.narration: Return to New Unit and name the vehicle Training Only, Community Van, with the exercise date. Select the new type and station. Add two positions with different names. Coordination Seat requires the existing Community Response Navigator personnel role, and its Required box is checked. Optional Support Seat has no personnel-role restriction and its Required box is clear. These are the unit’s seat definitions. No person is assigned by creating either row.

scenes.title: Inspect staffing without changing assignments
scenes.narration: Open Unit Staffing to distinguish positions from assigned people. Engine fifty-one retains Herrmann in its one configured seat. The new van is Not Staffed, and both positions are Not Occupied. Opening a person selector does not itself prove that the listed people hold the required role. We close it without selecting anyone. Save on this page replaces staffing selections across the department, so we leave it untouched and preserve every existing assignment.

These tree choices filter the view; they do not move a unit, assign a crew member, or change its status.

scenes.title: Apply the structure across sectors
scenes.narration: Chicago Fire can separate a coordination structure from a station and its vehicles. Community care and mental health teams can organize operational teams and bases without patient detail. Search and rescue can distinguish coordination groups, staging bases, and resources; security teams can structure patrol resources; wildland teams can organize seasonal bases; and industrial response teams can separate facility groups from response vehicles. In each setting, verify saved relationships and seat requirements, then manage actual staffing as a separate, deliberate operation.
